chapters.summary: Jonah disobeys God's command and flees toward Tarshish; along the way he runs into a violent storm, is thrown into the sea by the sailors, and is swallowed by a great fish.
keyPoints: The word of the LORD comes to Jonah, sending him to Nineveh to proclaim a warning.
Jonah instead boards a ship bound for Tarshish, fleeing from the presence of the LORD.
A violent storm rises on the sea; Jonah confesses that he fears God, is thrown overboard, and a great fish swallows him.
chapters.application: When we run from God's will, storms often follow. But God remains sovereign even in the storm, and his mercy will surely reach us. May we learn to obey and turn back to him without delay.

chapters.summary: From the belly of the fish, Jonah prays to God, giving thanks for his salvation and vowing to offer thanksgiving; at last God commands the fish to vomit Jonah out onto dry land.
keyPoints: From the belly of the fish, Jonah cries out to God, and the LORD hears his voice.
Jonah acknowledges his desperate situation, yet firmly believes that God will save him.
Jonah offers thanksgiving and vows to pay what he has promised, and God delivers him.
chapters.application: No matter how desperate our situation, we can cry out to God, and he will hear us. Let us give thanks even in hardship, keep the promises we make, and know his salvation.

chapters.summary: At God's second call, Jonah goes to Nineveh and preaches; the whole city, from the greatest to the least, repents, and God relents from sending disaster.
keyPoints: God calls Jonah a second time, and this time Jonah obeys and goes to Nineveh.
Jonah proclaims the message of judgment; the people of Nineveh believe God and declare a fast, turning from their sin.
God sees their repentance and relents from the disaster he had planned to bring.
chapters.application: No matter how we have failed in the past, God is still willing to give us another chance. When we truly repent, God will meet us with mercy.

chapters.summary: Jonah is angry and displeased that God does not destroy Nineveh after its repentance; through the gourd and the scorching heat, God teaches him what mercy really means.
keyPoints: Jonah is greatly displeased and angry with God for forgiving the people of Nineveh.
Through the gourd and the scorching heat, God leads Jonah to feel his own heart for cherishing living things.
God points out that Jonah cares about the gourd, yet is unwilling for God to show mercy to the hundred and twenty thousand people of Nineveh.
chapters.application: When we are displeased with God's grace, let us examine whether we value our own feelings more than God's heart, and learn to share his heart of mercy for others.
